skill.name: azure-resource-lookup
skill.description: Find and summarize Azure resources across subscriptions or resource groups using dedicated Azure MCP tools and read-only Azure Resource Graph queries.
skill.summary: Discover Azure resource inventories, tags, health states, and orphaned assets across scoped subscriptions.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Two findings are confirmed because the workflow generates and runs an Azure CLI command from user intent without an explicit validation or confirmation checkpoint. The other 29 detections are Markdown syntax, tool names, flags, or read-only examples, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: A command generated from user intent is executed without an explicit validation or approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Require review and user confirmation before execution. Allow only structured az graph query arguments and reject shell operators.

content.value_statement: Azure estates are difficult to inventory across subscriptions and resource types. This skill builds scoped, read-only Azure Resource Graph queries and presents focused results.
actual_capabilities: Lists Azure resources across one or more subscriptions or resource groups.
Selects dedicated Azure MCP tools when they provide complete coverage.
Builds read-only Azure Resource Graph queries from a stated inventory goal.
Finds untagged, unhealthy, failed, or potentially orphaned resources using documented KQL patterns.
Formats selected resource fields as concise tables.
Explains common authorization, extension, syntax, and empty-result errors.
limitations: Requires authenticated Azure access and sufficient RBAC permissions.
Azure Resource Graph data can lag and is unsuitable for real-time monitoring.
Results depend on the selected subscription scope and query limits.
Does not deploy resources, change configuration, or perform cost optimization.

use_cases.title: Build a cloud inventory
use_cases.description: List resources by type, location, subscription, and resource group for operational reviews.

use_cases.title: Investigate resource health
use_cases.description: Find failed provisioning states, unavailable resources, and active service incidents across selected subscriptions.

use_cases.title: Audit tags and orphaned assets
use_cases.description: Identify missing tags, unattached disks, unused public IP addresses, and orphaned network interfaces.

prompt_templates.title: List web apps
prompt_templates.prompt: List all Azure web apps in subscription [subscription]. Show name, resource group, location, state, and plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one resource type

prompt_templates.title: Summarize resource inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Count Azure resources by type across subscriptions [subscriptions]. Sort by highest count and identify the largest categories.

prompt_templates.title: Check required tags
prompt_templates.prompt: Find resources in [subscriptions] missing Environment or CostCenter tags. Group results by resource type and resource group.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze orphaned resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Find unattached disks, unused public IP addresses, and orphaned network interfaces in [subscriptions]. Use separate scoped queries and summarize deletion candidates.

output_examples.input: List web apps in the production subscription.
output: Found 18 App Services across five resource groups.
The table includes each app name, state, location, resource group, and App Service plan.

output_examples.input: Count resources by type across two subscriptions.
output: The subscriptions contain 426 resources across 31 resource types.
Storage accounts, network interfaces, and managed disks are the largest categories.
Counts are grouped by subscription for comparison.

output_examples.input: Find resources missing the Environment tag.
output: Found 42 resources without the Environment tag.
Results are grouped by resource type and resource group.

best_practices: Confirm the intended subscriptions and resource groups before running broad queries.
Use dedicated MCP tools for supported single-resource requests.
Limit result counts and project only fields needed for the decision.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated commands before reviewing their scope and arguments.
Do not use Azure Resource Graph for real-time monitoring or resource changes.
Do not treat orphaned-resource matches as deletion approval.

faq.question: What Azure access is required?
faq.answer: The user needs authenticated Azure access and read permission for every subscription or resource group included in the query.

faq.question: Does this skill modify resources?
faq.answer: No. It uses read-only discovery workflows and does not deploy, update, or delete Azure resources.

faq.question: Can it search multiple subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. Azure Resource Graph can query selected subscriptions when the authenticated identity has access.

faq.question: How current are the results?
faq.answer: Azure Resource Graph is near real time, but indexed metadata can have a short delay.

faq.question: Can it identify orphaned resources?
faq.answer: It identifies candidates from metadata patterns. Validate dependencies and ownership before taking deletion actions.

faq.question: Does it provide cost optimization?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated Azure cost analysis workflow for pricing, savings, or optimization decisions.
